subject: history
angle: The tobacco industry uses a variety of tactics, including misleading arguments, lobbying, and the creation of front organizations, to deliberately manipulate scientific information and undermine public health policies.
title: The Manufacture of Doubt

hooks.text: Who is funding the science you read?
You think it is a debate. It is a manufacture.
You trust the facts. They are being edited.
A boardroom meeting in a glass tower.

reveal.headline: The tobacco industry deliberately alters knowable facts for profit.
reveal.body: Research shows they misrepresent empirical evidence to promote their own agenda. They create front organizations to obscure their involvement in science.

explain.headline: Manufacturing doubt through systematic tactics.
explain.body: The industry uses misleading arguments, lobbying, and alliances with other sectors to influence marketing regulations. They use pricing strategies to undermine tax policies.

matters.headline: Why you see what they want you to see.
matters.body: That may be why public health policies feel like a constant debate. Information you trust may be shaped by those who profit from the status quo.

example.headline: A news scroll on your phone.
example.body: You read a report on public health and see a debate about new regulations. You see different sides arguing over the same data point.

question.headline: Who owns the information you trust?

stat.label: how the tobacco industry treats knowable facts

claims.text: The Foundation for a Smoke-Free World produces tobacco industry-friendly research and obscures industry involvement in science.
claims.quote: producing tobacco industry-friendly research and opinion; obscuring industry involvement in science; funding third parties which denigrate science and scientists that may threaten industry profitability; and promoting tobacco industry credibility.

claims.text: The tobacco industry uses sophisticated pricing strategies to undermine tax policies and increase profits.
claims.quote: the TI widely uses a multitude of sophisticated pricing strategies across different settings around the world with the intention of undermining tax policies, thereby increasing tobacco consumption and maximising their profits.

claims.text: Tobacco industry data on the illicit tobacco trade are not reliable due to a lack of transparency in data collection and presentation.
claims.quote: Lack of transparency from data collection right through to presentation of findings was a key issue with insufficient information to allow replication of the findings frequently cited.

claims.text: The tobacco industry has deliberately altered and misrepresented knowable facts and empirical evidence to promote an agenda for monetary benefit.
claims.quote: Numerous groups, such as the tobacco industry, have deliberately altered and misrepresented knowable facts and empirical evidence to promote an agenda, often for monetary benefit

claims.text: The tobacco industry uses direct and indirect lobbying, voluntary codes, and alliances with other industrial sectors to influence marketing regulations.
claims.quote: The industry primarily conveys these arguments through direct and indirect lobbying, the promotion of voluntary codes and alternative policies, and the formation of alliances with other industrial sectors.

claims.text: The tobacco industry has historically tried to keep tobacco taxes low using consistent tactics and misleading arguments.
claims.quote: The tobacco industry has historically tried to keep tobacco taxes low using consistent tactics and misleading arguments.

verdict: The sources provide consistent evidence that the tobacco industry employs diverse, systematic strategies to manufacture doubt and influence regulations for profit.
caveat: While the tactics are well-documented, the sources do not provide a comprehensive list of every specific scientific fact that has been misrepresented.
caption:
The tobacco industry uses systematic tactics to shape public perception. 

Research shows they use lobbying, front organizations, and the misrepresentation of facts to influence regulations. The evidence does not provide a comprehensive list of every specific fact they have altered. 

What other industries might be shaping your view of the world?
